savings_or_continuation_provisions.quote: Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect: (i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or (ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
savings_or_continuation_provisions.note: Standard no-impair clause. It protects statutory agency authority and OMB functions, not the provisions, offices or actions of the revoked orders, so it saves nothing of the 7 batch orders.

savings_or_continuation_provisions.quote: shall review all Federal Government actions taken pursuant to the orders, memoranda, and proclamations listed in section 2 of this order and take necessary steps to rescind, replace, or amend such actions as appropriate
savings_or_continuation_provisions.note: A review-and-rescind directive to the DPC and NEC Directors. It implies that agency actions already taken under a listed order are not voided by the revocation itself, but it is not a savings clause: it preserves no provision, office or right of any revoked order.

effective_date_reading: Sec. 2 says 'The following executive actions are hereby revoked' and the order has no effective-date, delayed-effect or phase-in wording anywhere (secs. 1-4 read in full). The revocations therefore took effect on signing, January 20, 2025 (printed 90 FR 8237-8241, January 28, 2025).
conclusion: EO 14148 (signed 2025-01-20, 90 FR 8237-8241, PDF pages 1-5, read once in full) revokes 78 listed executive actions in sec. 2(a)-(zzz), including EO 14009 (t), 14044 (ll), 14049 (nn), 14070 (uu), 14087 (zz), 14089 (aaa) and 14099 (fff). It has no effective-date wording, so each revocation is effective on signing. Sec. 3 directs agencies to end implementation, tells the DPC and NEC Directors to review and rescind actions taken under the listed orders and to propose more rescissions within 45 days, and tells the National Security Advisor to review NSMs. Sec. 4 is a general no-impair clause for statutory authority and OMB functions, plus no-private-rights language. There is no successor delegation, no transfer of functions, funds or property, no pending-matter clause and no exception for any listed order. Whether a revoked order leaves its own residual (completed acts on other orders, offices or rights) therefore depends on the order read, not on EO 14148. EO 14148 does not say whether the revocations revive anything the listed orders had revoked, so the general non-revival rule governs those.

batch_03_addendum.reader_question_answer: Each of the 8 targets is revoked in whole by sec. 2 effective on signing, 2025-01-20 (the printed date 2025-01-28 is the FR publication date, not an effective date). EO 14148 saves no function, office, right or pending matter of any listed order and transfers nothing; sec. 3(b) only directs review and rescission of agency actions taken under them.
